distractors.reason: 'Look at' means to turn your eyes toward something. We don't say 'look at my sister' to mean take care of her.
'Look for' means to search for something you lost. It doesn't mean caring for a person.
'Look to' is not used with this meaning. We don't say 'look to my sister' to mean take care of her.

example_sentence: My grandmother looks ___ my little sister every afternoon.
l1_interference: Los hispanohablantes pueden traducir 'cuidar a' de forma literal con 'look at', pero 'look at' solo significa mirar algo con los ojos. Para cuidar a alguien en inglés se usa 'look after'.
explanation: In English, 'look after' means to take care of a person, an animal, or a thing. The preposition 'after' shows that you are responsible for someone's needs.

related_collocations.example: My mom takes care of the dog.
I talk to my brother every day.

memory_tip: LOOK AFTER = take care of a person | LOOK AT = watch something with your eyes
